text: 🚨🇲🇽 "We are against any form of racism, and even more so when it comes to our compatriots in the United States. [...] For us, they are heroes." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 On Sunday another Mexican national died in a US immigration detention center. He had been detained in June; his family said he suffered from diabetes and hypertension and probably did not have all his medications. The Foreign Ministry contacted the family, issued a statement and will file a complaint in the United States, and consulates will reinforce protection of detainees' human rights. The question was about Los Tigres del Norte, whose song says "I didn't cross the border, the border crossed me." Sheinbaum hosted them at the National Palace, a first for a Mexican president. They turn 50 next year.

text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "Otherwise regular gasoline would be over 30 pesos and diesel over 35. Look at what is happening in various countries of the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 Mexico cut the tax on fuel and signed a voluntary agreement with gas station owners. Consumer agency Profeco reports an average diesel price of 26.98 pesos a liter, with 87.8% of stations under the 27-peso cap. Profeco is now inspecting stations selling premium at nearly 30 pesos, a 5-peso margin on fuel that also gets a tax stimulus. "The fiscal stimulus is for the people, not for the gas station owner to earn more money," said Profeco head Iván Escalante.

🇲🇽🛢️ "Companies had grown used to treating the Spanish-American countries as simple colonies of exploitation, becoming economic powers above the sovereign power of the states." — Lázaro Cárdenas, March 12, 1939, read at the Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 Cárdenas died on October 19, 1970, 56 years ago today. The mañanera's new Humanismo Mexicano segment, presented by Joseline Morales, recalled his record: 18 million hectares handed to 800,000 peasants and Indigenous people, 40 national parks, and the founding of the IPN, El Colegio de México and INAH. He also took in Spanish Republican exiles. In 1938 the foreign oil companies defied a Supreme Court ruling for the oil workers, and he nationalized the industry: "our second independence, economic independence."

🇲🇽🏭 "Do you know why they come to Mexico? Not only because we're close to the United States. We no longer boast cheap labor. We boast the great engineers, young men and women, this country has." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 Mexican manufacturing rebounded in August to its highest level in three years. Sheinbaum said the auto industry has recovered after taking a hit, and electronics is growing with new jobs. Mexico is among the countries that graduate the most engineers. "That is what many companies are looking for."

🇲🇽🎨 "400,000 more young people in high school: the best way to address the causes of violence." "The best policy: more education, more school places, more scholarships that let young people stay in school." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 19, 2026 Scholarship coordinator Julio León said about 1.5 million first-year students usually apply for the Benito Juárez high-school scholarship. This year nearly 400,000 more did, as new high schools open. The scholarship system now covers 19,593,156 students with 136.9 billion pesos in 2026, and aims for 22 million by year's end. Thanks to early enrollment uploads, payments to high school and university students began today instead of in December.

🇲🇽🏦 <u>Record 1.66 Million Mexicans Dip Into Their Afores for Unemployment</u>

In the first nine months of 2026, 1.66 million workers made unemployment withdrawals from their private pension accounts, taking out more than 36 billion pesos, a record for the period, according to Consar data reported by El Economista. The amount withdrawn rose 30% year over year and the average withdrawal hit 21,877 pesos.

Consar blames unlicensed "coyotes" who inflate withdrawals for a commission and drain workers' contribution weeks. Afore Azteca leads with 8,023 million pesos withdrawn. The Afores were created in 1997 under Zedillo.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Another Mexican Dies in ICE Custody. That Makes 18 Since Trump Returned</u>

Mexico's Foreign Ministry is demanding that the United States clarify the death of Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias, 56, who died at ICE's Río Grande processing center in Laredo, Texas. He is the 18th Mexican national to die in US immigration custody or operations since January 20, 2025.

The SRE is asking for a prompt, exhaustive and transparent investigation, will file a complaint with the Webb County district attorney, and is demanding consular access to detention centers to check on medical conditions.
